title: LORD JESUS, STRETCH FORTH YOUR HAND AND TOUCH ME AS YOU TOUCHED THE LEPER
text: Hallelujah. Somebody shout hallelujah like you mean it. Not like church etiquette, like a man on the ground who just watched the hand move toward him. I want you to hold your own hand right now. Hold it. Look at it. This is the same kind of hand he stretched forth. Flesh, fingers, ordinary looking. And yet when that hand which is really the hand of God wrapped in human skin reached toward a man that society had already buried alive, everything changed. I want to take you into a story you think you know because I believe most of us have read Matthew chapter 8 and Mark chapter 1 so many times that the shock of it has worn off. Tonight the spirit of God wants to put the shock back in. Matthew chapter 8:2 says, "And behold, there came a leper and worshipped him saying, 'Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.'" Mark chapter 1:41 continues the story and says, "And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand and touched him and saith unto him, 'I will. Be thou clean.'" Put those two verses together and something detonates in your spirit. A leper worshipped before he was healed. He didn't wait for the miracle to bow. He bowed while still covered in the disease. Somebody here needs to hear that. You do not need to wait until your situation changes before you worship. Worship is not the response to breakthrough. Sometimes worship is the door through which breakthrough walks in. I want to teach you something about leprosy in that culture because if you don't understand the culture, you will not understand the miracle. A leper in that society was not simply sick. He was excommunicated. Leviticus chapter 13:45 and 46 laid out the law plainly. "The leprous man must dwell alone outside the camp, his clothes torn, his head bare, and he must cry 'Unclean, unclean' so that no one would come near him by accident. Do you hear that? The law required him to announce his own disqualification everywhere he went. He was the loneliest man in Israel. Not because he chose isolation, but because isolation was legislated upon him. Nobody touched him. Nobody hugged him. Nobody shook his hand. His own family, if they loved him, loved him from a distance because to come close was to become unclean also. I am prophesying right now that there is a soul in this place. Maybe watching this from your phone. Maybe sitting in the back row. Who has become so used to shouting unclean, unclean over your own life that you now believe it is your identity. You've said it about your marriage. You've said it about your finances. You've said it about your body. You've said it about your ministry, your gifting, your future. You have declared yourself unclean so many times that it has become your personal prophecy over your own life. And tonight the Holy Ghost is interrupting that broadcast. Say this out loud with me. I am not what rejection named me. I am not what shame labeled me. I am what the hand of Jesus is about to call me. Now here is the part that should make you tremble. This leper, in defiance of the law, in defiance of culture, in defiance of every voice that had ever told him to stay back, walked toward Jesus. He broke protocol to reach for mercy. Somebody needs to understand tonight that sometimes your healing requires you to break the protocol of your own shame. You have been observing the rules of your rejection for so long. The rule that says don't hope too much. The rule that says don't ask again. You already asked and nothing happened. The rule that says stay in your lane. Stay in your corner. Stay outside the camp. Tonight I release a grace upon somebody to break that protocol and press toward him the way that leper pressed toward him. And what did Jesus do? This is the verse that undoes me every time. He could have healed him with a word from a distance. He had done that before with the Centurion's servant in Matthew chapter 8 verse 13. He spoke and the servant was healed in the selfsame hour without Jesus ever visiting the house. So, we know Jesus did not need proximity to release power. He could have shouted from 20 ft away, "Be clean." And the leprosy would have obeyed, but he didn't. Mark tells us he put forth his hand. He closed the distance himself. He walked into the leper's contamination zone. Under the law, when a clean person touched an unclean person, the clean person became unclean. That was the mathematics of that old covenant. But when the hand of Jesus touched the leprosy, the mathematics reversed. >> [music] >> Instead of holiness becoming contaminated, contamination became holy. Instead of the clean man catching the disease, the disease man caught the cleanness. Hallelujah. Somebody needs to shout at what I just said because that is the whole gospel in one sentence. Under every other religion, uncleanness spreads and contaminates purity. Under grace, purity spreads and contaminates uncleanness. That is why 2 Corinthians chapter 5 verse 21 says, "For he had made him to be sin for us who knew no sin." That we might be made the righteousness of God in him. He did not just avoid catching your sin. He absorbed it so that his righteousness could become contagious to you. I feel something rising in this room. There is a fire gathering. Let the sound go up. If you understand what I just said, don't sit there quietly. Something in the spirit realm just shifted for somebody's health. Lift your hands and receive it.
